title: PM Modi Begins Three-Nation Tour: Indonesia, New Zealand, and Australia
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi commenced a three-nation diplomatic visit beginning with Indonesia (Jakarta), followed by New Zealand and Australia. His aircraft was escorted by Indonesian fighter jets upon arrival in Jakarta. The agenda includes defence cooperation, critical minerals, and strategic partnership discussions. India is also reportedly eyeing a uranium supply pact with Australia during the visit.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 2 (IR): covers India's bilateral ties with ASEAN (Indonesia), Pacific nations, and the Quad partner Australia; also relevant for India's civil nuclear energy push and critical minerals diplomacy.
key_facts: Three nations: Indonesia, New Zealand, Australia
Agenda: Defence, critical minerals, strategic ties
India eyeing uranium supply pact with Australia
Indonesia is India's key ASEAN partner; New Zealand PM Luxon called both 'natural partners'
source: The Hindu / Hindustan Times / Times of India

title: NIA Charges Hafiz Saeed in Pahalgam Terror Attack Case
summary: India's National Investigation Agency (NIA) has filed charges against Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba chief Hafiz Saeed in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack case. The move marks a significant step in India's legal pursuit of designated terrorists based in Pakistan. Hafiz Saeed is already on the FATF-linked terrorism financing watchlist and is designated as a global terrorist by the UN.
exam_angle: Relevant for internal security and IR: NIA's mandate under the NIA Act 2008, India-Pakistan terrorism-related disputes, and India's counter-terror legal framework.
key_facts: Agency: National Investigation Agency (NIA)
Accused: Hafiz Saeed, LeT chief based in Pakistan
Case: Pahalgam terror attack
Saeed is a UN-designated global terrorist

title: Pakistan's Bilawal Bhutto Threatens War Over Indus Waters Treaty
summary: Pakistan People's Party (PPP) leader Bilawal Bhutto Zardari threatened India with war, stating Pakistan is 'ready on all fronts' over the dispute regarding the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). India had suspended the IWT in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. The Indus Waters Treaty, brokered by the World Bank in 1960, governs sharing of six Indus basin rivers between India and Pakistan.
exam_angle: Critical for GS Paper 2 (IR): Indus Waters Treaty provisions, India's suspension of IWT post-Pahalgam, and implications for India-Pakistan water diplomacy.
key_facts: Indus Waters Treaty signed: 1960, brokered by World Bank
India suspended IWT following Pahalgam terror attack
IWT allocates western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan; eastern rivers to India
Bilawal Bhutto is PPP chairman and former Pakistan Foreign Minister

title: New Zealand PM Christopher Luxon Addresses Khalistan Issue, Reaffirms India Ties
summary: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon stated that the Khalistan issue 'caused suffering in India' and that New Zealand would not tolerate criminal behaviour or intimidation. He called India and New Zealand 'natural partners' ahead of PM Modi's visit to Wellington. Luxon's remarks are significant given concerns over Khalistani activities on New Zealand soil affecting bilateral relations.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR): India's diaspora-related security concerns abroad, Five Eyes nations' stance on Sikh separatism, and India-New Zealand bilateral relations.
key_facts: NZ PM: Christopher Luxon
Statement: Will not tolerate Khalistan-linked criminal behaviour
Context: PM Modi's three-nation tour includes New Zealand
India-NZ described as 'natural partners'

title: India Orders Meta to Remove Child Sexual Abuse Ads on Instagram
summary: The Indian government directed Meta to remove advertisements on Instagram that were found to be promoting child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The order reflects India's growing regulatory assertiveness over social media intermediaries under the IT Act and IT Rules 2021. The action deepens Meta's regulatory challenges in India following previous content moderation controversies.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (Governance): IT Act 2000, Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code Rules 2021, and protection of children online (POCSO Act linkages).
key_facts: Platform: Instagram (Meta)
Issue: Ads promoting child sexual abuse material (CSAM)
Legal framework: IT Act 2000 and IT Rules 2021
India is Meta's largest market by user base

title: Hamas Dissolves Gaza Governing Body, Offers Transfer to UN/US-Backed Committee
summary: Hamas announced the dissolution of its governing body in Gaza, offering to transfer administrative authority to a UN and US-backed committee. Israel responded by demanding Hamas disarm, calling the move 'tricks.' The development comes amid ongoing ceasefire negotiations and international pressure for a post-war governance framework in Gaza.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR): West Asia conflict dynamics, India's stated position of supporting a two-state solution, and UN-mediated governance frameworks.
key_facts: Hamas dissolved its Gaza governing body (Political Bureau-linked administration)
Transfer proposed to UN/US-backed committee
Israel demands Hamas disarmament as precondition
Context: Ongoing Israel-Gaza conflict post-October 2023

title: Khamenei Funeral: Trump Warns Iran — 'Will Finish the Job' If No Deal
summary: US President Donald Trump issued a fresh warning to Iran amid the state funeral of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, saying the US will either make a nuclear deal with Iran or 'finish the job.' Iran's Embassy in India expressed gratitude to the Indian government for participating in Khamenei's funeral. The statements signal continued high tensions in the US-Iran nuclear standoff.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR): Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA) history, India-Iran relations, Chabahar port strategic interest, and West Asia geopolitics.
key_facts: Iran Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's funeral held
Trump: US will either make deal or 'finish the job'
India represented at Khamenei's funeral (Iran Embassy expressed gratitude)
Context: JCPOA negotiations remain stalled

title: Extradition of Nirav Modi Imminent After Loss at European Court of Human Rights
summary: Fugitive diamantaire Nirav Modi is expected to be extradited to India soon after losing his appeal at the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR). Nirav Modi is wanted in India in connection with the Punjab National Bank (PNB) fraud case estimated at over Rs 13,500 crore. He has been held in a UK prison while contesting extradition proceedings.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) and GS Paper 3 (Economy): extradition treaties, India-UK bilateral legal cooperation, banking fraud, and fugitive economic offenders.
key_facts: Nirav Modi: Accused in PNB fraud (Rs 13,500+ crore)
Court: European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against him
Currently held in UK prison
Relevant law: Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018

title: Congress Challenges Meenakshi Natarajan's Rajya Sabha Nomination Rejection in High Court
summary: The Indian National Congress has announced it will move the High Court challenging the rejection of its nominee Meenakshi Natarajan's Rajya Sabha nomination. The dispute raises questions about the constitutional process for Rajya Sabha elections and the role of the Election Commission in scrutinising nomination papers. Natarajan is a senior Congress leader from Madhya Pradesh.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (Polity): Articles 80 and 84 on Rajya Sabha membership eligibility, nomination process, and judicial review of election matters.
key_facts: Nominee: Meenakshi Natarajan (Congress, Madhya Pradesh)
House: Rajya Sabha
Action: Congress to approach High Court
Relevant Articles: Article 80 (Rajya Sabha composition), Article 84 (qualification)

title: Assam Rifles Soldiers Killed in Militant Ambush in Manipur's Ukhrul
summary: Two Assam Rifles personnel were killed and several others injured after militants ambushed a convoy in Ukhrul district of Manipur. The Assam Rifles, operating under the dual command of the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Indian Army, is the oldest paramilitary force of India. Manipur has seen sustained ethnic violence and insurgency since May 2023.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Internal Security): Assam Rifles' mandate under AFSPA, insurgency in Northeast India, and the ongoing Manipur conflict situation.
key_facts: Force: Assam Rifles (oldest paramilitary, dual control: MHA + Army)
Location: Ukhrul district, Manipur
Casualties: 2 soldiers killed, several injured
Context: Manipur ethnic violence ongoing since May 2023

title: NSE Targets Rs 30,000 Crore IPO Launch in September
summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has set a target to launch its Initial Public Offering (IPO) worth Rs 30,000 crore in September. NSE's IPO has been long-awaited pending SEBI clearance following the co-location scam investigations. NSE is the world's largest derivatives exchange by volume and India's largest equity exchange.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy): capital markets regulation, SEBI's role, IPO process, and the significance of NSE's listing for market deepening.
key_facts: NSE IPO target size: Rs 30,000 crore
Target launch: September
NSE: world's largest derivatives exchange by volume
Regulator: SEBI clearance pending due to co-location scam probe

title: India's Trade Deficit with Japan Triples in 10 Years; FTA Review Underway
summary: India's trade deficit with Japan has tripled over the past decade, raising concerns about the effectiveness of the India-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) signed in 2011. A review of the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is currently underway to rebalance trade flows and attract greater Japanese investment into India. Japan is a key investor in India's infrastructure and automobile sectors.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy) and GS Paper 2 (IR): India-Japan CEPA, trade deficit management, and the broader debate on India's FTA outcomes.
key_facts: India-Japan CEPA signed: 2011
Trade deficit with Japan tripled in 10 years
FTA review ongoing to boost investments
Japan is a major investor in Indian infrastructure and automobile sector

title: World Bank Updates Income Classification: Vietnam and 5 Others Move Up; India's Status
summary: The World Bank released its updated income classification of countries, with Vietnam and five other nations climbing to higher income brackets. India continues to be classified as a lower-middle-income country in the World Bank's groupings based on Gross National Income (GNI) per capita. The World Bank uses the Atlas method for GNI per capita calculation to classify countries annually.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy): World Bank income classification thresholds (low, lower-middle, upper-middle, high income), India's per capita income position, and development benchmarks.
key_facts: World Bank classifies countries by GNI per capita (Atlas method)
Vietnam among 6 nations moving up in income classification
India remains: lower-middle-income country
Four income groups: Low, Lower-middle, Upper-middle, High income

title: UP Cabinet Approves Startup Policy 2026 with Rs 15 Lakh Seed Funding
summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved the Startup Policy 2026, which includes a provision of Rs 15 lakh seed funding for new ventures. The policy aims to boost the startup ecosystem in India's most populous state by providing financial and regulatory support to early-stage entrepreneurs. UP is targeting to become a top startup destination to compete with states like Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy/Schemes): state-level startup ecosystem policies, seed funding mechanisms, and India's overall startup promotion framework (Startup India).
key_facts: Policy: UP Startup Policy 2026
Approved by: Uttar Pradesh Cabinet
Key provision: Rs 15 lakh seed funding per new venture
Complements Central Government's Startup India initiative (launched 2016)

title: Hyderabad Startup Prepares for World's First Soft Robotic Orbital Capture Demonstration
summary: A Hyderabad-based startup is preparing to conduct the world's first demonstration of soft robotic capture technology in Earth's orbit. The mission is aimed at addressing the growing problem of space debris by using flexible, soft robotic systems to capture defunct satellites and debris. This positions India's private space sector at the frontier of in-orbit servicing and debris mitigation technology.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech): India's private space sector under IN-SPACe framework, space debris mitigation, and active debris removal (ADR) technologies.
key_facts: Startup based in Hyderabad, India
Mission: World's first soft robotic capture demonstration in orbit
Purpose: Space debris mitigation / active debris removal
Regulatory body: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre)

title: India's Power Demand to Grow 6% Annually Over Next 4-5 Years: Centrum Report
summary: A report by Centrum Research projects that India's power demand will grow at approximately 6% annually over the next four to five years. The growth is expected to be driven by rapid industrialisation, rising urban demand, electric vehicle adoption, and data centre proliferation. India is currently the third-largest electricity producer and consumer in the world.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 3 (Economy/Energy): India's energy security, power sector reforms, renewable energy targets, and the PM Surya Ghar and National Electricity Plan 2032 context.
key_facts: Projected power demand growth: ~6% per annum
Period: Next 4-5 years
Report by: Centrum Research
India: 3rd largest electricity producer and consumer globally

title: Sonam Wangchuk's Hunger Strike Enters Day 9 Over Ladakh Statehood Demand
summary: Climate activist and Magsaysay Award winner Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike entered its ninth day as he continues to demand full statehood and Sixth Schedule protections for the Union Territory of Ladakh. Wangchuk has previously led the 'Leh Chalo' march and has been a prominent voice for protecting the tribal and ecological rights of Ladakh's indigenous communities. Ladakh became a Union Territory without a legislature on 31 October 2019 following the reorganisation of Jammu & Kashmir.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (Polity): Sixth Schedule of the Constitution (tribal area protection), UT governance without legislature, Article 3 (reorganisation of states), and Ladakh's political status.
key_facts: Activist: Sonam Wangchuk (Ramon Magsaysay Award winner)
Demand: Statehood and Sixth Schedule protection for Ladakh
Ladakh became UT (without legislature) on 31 October 2019
Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in NE India; Ladakh seeks its inclusion

title: Venezuela Earthquake Death Toll Rises to 3,535 — Places in News
summary: The death toll from a major earthquake in Venezuela has risen to 3,535, with over 16,700 people reported injured. Venezuela, located in northern South America, lies on the Caribbean tectonic plate boundary, making it seismically active. The disaster has triggered international humanitarian response calls.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 1 (Geography): seismic zones of South America, Caribbean plate tectonics, and disaster management frameworks. Also useful for 'places in news' questions.
key_facts: Country: Venezuela (northern South America)
Death toll: 3,535; Injured: 16,700+
Cause: Major earthquake
Venezuela sits on Caribbean-South American plate boundary

title: Xi Jinping Confirmed to Visit United States in September: Trump
summary: US President Donald Trump announced that Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit the United States in September. The visit is expected to cover ongoing US-China trade tensions, tariff negotiations, and broader geopolitical disputes including Taiwan, South China Sea, and technology competition. The announcement comes amid a period of cautious diplomatic re-engagement after earlier tariff escalations.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR): US-China relations, trade war dynamics, implications for India's strategic positioning in the Indo-Pacific, and Quad context.
key_facts: Xi Jinping to visit USA in September (per Trump announcement)
Agenda: Trade, tariffs, geopolitical issues
Context: Ongoing US-China trade tensions and tariff war
Significant for Indo-Pacific balance of power

title: Netanyahu Asks US Not to Sell F-35 Jets to Turkey Over Regional Power Balance
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has formally requested the United States not to sell F-35 stealth fighter jets to Turkey, citing concerns over the regional 'power balance.' Turkey was previously removed from the F-35 programme in 2019 after purchasing Russia's S-400 missile defence system. The development reflects ongoing tensions within NATO over Turkey's strategic alignments.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Defence): F-35 technology transfer politics, NATO cohesion, US arms export policy (ITAR), and Israel-Turkey-US triangle.
key_facts: F-35: 5th-generation stealth multirole fighter (Lockheed Martin, USA)
Turkey excluded from F-35 programme in 2019 due to S-400 purchase from Russia
Netanyahu's request: Block F-35 sale to Turkey
Concern: Regional power balance in Middle East/Eastern Mediterranean
